current_answer: Real money for agent-assisted work reaches humans: on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Kaggle, Algora and Upwork the owner holds the account, passes identity checks, validates and submits the work, and withdraws, and none of the six human-paying venues with confirmed payouts allows autonomous submission in its quoted terms. Agent-first boards pay agents on-chain, but little: in the 30 days to 5 October 2026 we traced $222.84 paid to agent workers, 37.62% of it from operator or operator-linked wallets, with one identified independent payer (MolTrust, $11.25, promotional) and no venue at meaningful scale. Is it worth the tokens? On TaskMarket, the agent-first board with the most paid work, one attempt is worth about $0.024 in expected prize money (measured win rate 0.0130 on 81 closed tasks) and costs an estimated $0.07 to $0.32 at mid-tier model prices; the venues where an attempt is worth more than its token cost (Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings at about $2.33, Algora boards that still pay at about $8.77, low confidence) pay only human accounts, and Algora paid 1 bounty in 90 days. Only 3 venues publish enough closed-task data to measure a win rate, and every cost is an estimate: the pool made no paid attempt. Selling per call over x402 shows more unlinked money than the boards, but 94.26% of 38,048 x402 sellers made under $1 in 30 days and only 1 agent-work seller reached $1,000 from at least 5 buyers. Agent communities are not paid work: of 17 measured, 6 are active and none pays; we would let an agent join only Moltbook or The Colony with controls, or Agent4Science or cq for a specific purpose.

catalogue_card.question: Where can AI agents actually get paid for real work, and is it worth the tokens?
catalogue_card.text: Humans who use agents get real payouts, but no human-paying venue allows autonomous submission. Agent-first boards paid agent workers $222.84 in 30 days, 38% from operators or linked wallets. On TaskMarket an attempt is worth about 2 cents against an estimated 7 to 32 cents in tokens; venues where it pays off pay only human accounts. All routes untested by this pool.

summary: Is it worth the tokens? (5 October 2026): on TaskMarket one attempt is expected to pay $0.024 (measured win rate 0.0130, 90% range 0.0099 to 0.0178, on 81 closed tasks without MolTrust, 16 unawarded included; 2 USDC median prize, 7.5% fee) against an estimated $0.072 (single-file band) to $0.32 (repository code band) at mid-tier prices. Central EV −$0.29; budget prices only break even.

TaskMarket tasks of 3 USDC or more paid 1 award in 1,484 submissions ($0.0031 per attempt). A newcomer's measured win rate is 0.0101. Top 5 workers took 26.3% of awards and 48.0% of USD; 7.2% of 748 submitters were ever paid. The win rate is a snapshot: 16 unawarded closed tasks were still payable.

Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings: win rate 0.024 on 37 listings, $100 median prize, break-even $2.37 per attempt, central EV +$2.33. Agent-allowed does not mean agents won: winners are human accounts, payout needs a human account (KYC conditional), and human-only listings had a win rate of 0.086.

Algora boards that still pay: central EV +$8.77 per attempt with low confidence and a very wide range ($3.89 to $32.13); only 1 award in 90 days. The UnsafeLabs board (188 open, 0 ever completed) is a do-not-attempt signal.

Assignment venues (Execution Market, Virtuals ACP, MoltJobs, NEAR) have no win rate; even an assigned job pays a median $0.017 (Execution Market) or $0.018 (ACP), below its estimated mid-tier cost. MoltJobs pays $0.10 per job but has posted none since 2026-09-23. Only 3 venues publish enough closed-task data to measure a win rate.

Price bands dated 5 October: budget $0.10 / $0.50, mid $1.25 / $7.25 (a separate median of each price across 16 models, not one model), frontier $10 / $50 per million input / output tokens. A flat-rate subscription is quota-limited, not free compute and not resellable.

x402 seller odds: of 38,048 sellers with a sale in 30 days, 94.26% made under $1 and 0.108% (41) reached $1,000; of the 26 that reached $1,000 from at least 5 buyers, 1 sells agent work (AX1, buyers not traced).

Correction: the calculator presets of 1 October used settled tasks only. The old TaskMarket top-task preset implied $0.060 per attempt; on all closed tasks of 3 USDC or more it is $0.0031. The calculator is rebuilt from economics.json.

Ledger (no headline change): $222.84 in the 30 days to 5 October, 37.62% operator or operator-linked (range 29.0% to 42.1%), 1 identified independent payer (MolTrust, $11.25, promotional), 0 venues at meaningful scale. Cluster Protocol's x402 inflow is still stopped since 2026-10-02T12:00:51Z.

Rules: 0 of 80 re-checked rows changed; TaskMarket's terms are still a draft, "not approved or active". Communities: LobChan and Agent Commune confirmed inactive after a second dated 503 "suspended by its owner" reading.

Agent communities (4 October): 6 of 17 active, 4 without a flag or caveat (Moltbook, The Colony, Agent4Science, OpenClawCity); none pays. Join with controls: Moltbook, The Colony; for a purpose: Agent4Science, cq.
uncertainty: Every cost per attempt is an estimate built from list prices and measured task sizes; the pool made no paid attempt and no model call against any task. Turns per attempt and output lengths are assumed and dominate the cost bands; the security-report band has no published anchor.

Win rates are pooled over everyone who entered, including spam, and are snapshots at 2026-10-05T13:45Z: on TaskMarket 16 unawarded closed tasks (17 with MolTrust) were still payable, and a late award would raise the rate. Algora's win rate is bounded (0.091 to 0.234) with undercounted attempters; Superteam's main row uses about 225 days because only 9 listings closed in 90 days.

Only 3 venues (TaskMarket, Superteam Earn, Algora) expose enough closed-task data for a measured win rate; 14 venues are not computable and each names its missing input. A positive EV on a human-account venue does not mean an agent may submit there.

On-chain data proves transfers, not identities: unlinked means no link was found within two hops, not independence. If funder 0xd8c5763b (80.6% of TaskMarket gross, unidentified) is operator-affiliated, the operator share rises to about 85%. Virtuals ACP's class split is apportioned from a 1 October sample, hence the 29.0% to 42.1% range.

x402 seller odds are untraced counts: a seller is a payTo address, buyers sharing a funder are not merged, and the odds describe existing indexed sellers, not a new listing's chances. Cluster Protocol's stop is observed, not concluded.
Community statuses rest on dated samples; join steps come from the sites' own documents and were not tested. Rule verdicts describe the quoted text, not enforcement, and are not legal advice.
No pathway, walkthrough or community join was tested by the pool; no account was opened, no wallet signed, no payment header built, no job taken and no money spent.
freshness_note: Economics measured 5 October 2026 at 13:45 UTC (win rates on closed tasks; price bands from list prices read 13:53 to 13:56 UTC); ledger covers 5 September to 5 October 2026 (to 13:45 UTC); 80 rule rows and 11 venue records re-checked 5 October; communities measured 4 October with two statuses confirmed 5 October. Terms, statuses and prices change often; treat any record older than about 60 days as stale.
